newsitem.title: USA: Edison Palo Verde nuke settlement approved.
newsitem.headline: Edison Palo Verde nuke settlement approved.

text.p: Edison International's Southern Califoria Edison Co received approval Friday from the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to accelerate recovery of its remaining investment in an Arizona nuclear plant, the CPUC said.
Edison reached a settlement with consumer advocates in early November on recovery of the $1.2 billion investment, which the commission is now endorsing.

Edison is entitled to recover the balance of its sunk investment in the Palo Verde nuclear plant by the end of 2001, with a rate of return of 7.35 percent, compared with the previous rate of 9.55 percent.
This part of the agreement is nearly identical to a previous agreement on Edison's San Onofre nuclear plant, in which it is a majority owner and operator.
But Edison is only a 15.8 percent minority participant in the 3,700 megawatt Wintersburg, Ariz., nuclear facility, which is operated by Arizona Public Service Co.
As a result, the recovery of incremental operating costs for Palo Verde will be based on pass-through of actual costs, rather than fixed per-kilowatt hour costs as in the San Onofre settlement.
The CPUC estimated Edison will recover $375 million next year in sunk costs and operating expenses from Palo Verde.
The costs will be recovered in rates previously authorized by the CPUC since state law prohibits any rate increases for the next five years.
